questions.passage: Native Hawaiian fiber artist Marques Hanalei Marzan creates art using the techniques of lauhala weaving. Lauhala weaving is a traditional Hawaiian art form that uses leaves of the hala tree. Often, Marzan doesn’t have a specific [vocab]______[/vocab] what the final product will look like when he starts a new piece. Instead, he makes up his designs as he weaves, allowing inspiration to take him in unexpected directions.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.label: A
choices.text: acceptance of

choices.label: B
choices.text: imitation of

choices.label: C
choices.text: intention for

choices.label: D
choices.text: admiration for

explanation.key_evidence: Marzan “makes up his designs as he weaves.”
explanation.why_correct: Choice C fits because “intention for” means a plan or aim for how the final product will look.

choice_analysis.A: “Acceptance of” would describe approving the final product, not lacking a plan for it.
choice_analysis.B: “Imitation of” suggests copying something, but the passage says Marzan improvises.
choice_analysis.C: Correct. “Intention for” captures the idea of a specific plan for the final product.
choice_analysis.D: “Admiration for” means respect or appreciation, which is unrelated to planning a design.

explanation.short: Choice C is correct because Marzan begins without a predetermined plan for the artwork.
explanation.detailed: The passage says Marzan makes up designs as he weaves, so he does not have a specific aim for the final appearance. “Intention for” best expresses that meaning.

questions.passage: In a study at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, participants with clinically typical eyesight were shown a drawing of a broken line, with the break in the line situated in a blocked part of their field of vision. questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.label: A
choices.text: captivate

choices.label: B
choices.text: compensate

choices.label: C
choices.text: barricade

choices.label: D
choices.text: revert

explanation.key_evidence: The brain fills in missing visual information.
explanation.why_correct: Choice B fits because “compensate” means to make up for something incomplete or lacking.

choice_analysis.A: “Captivate” means attract attention, not fill in missing information.
choice_analysis.B: Correct. “Compensate” means make up for a deficiency, matching the brain’s response.
choice_analysis.C: “Barricade” means block, the opposite of filling in missing information.
choice_analysis.D: “Revert” means return to a previous state, which does not fit the process described.

explanation.short: Choice B is correct because the brain makes up for incomplete visual information.
explanation.detailed: Participants perceived the broken line as continuous even with missing visual input. The phrase “filling in what is missing” points directly to “compensate.”

questions.passage: Optimal foraging theory (OFT) holds that animals’ foraging behaviors reflect cost-benefit trade-offs that vary by species and with dynamic ecological circumstances. Wright found to be positively associated with foraging by three-striped night monkeys. choices.label: A

choices.label: C
choices.text: It may be weakened by the finding that the costs and benefits associated with a particular ecological circumstance vary by species.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It can account for observations of different species responding differently to similar ecological circumstances.

explanation.key_evidence: OFT explains why lunar intensity affects mice and monkeys differently.
explanation.why_correct: Choice D is correct because the passage uses OFT to account for different species responding differently to the same ecological circumstance.

choice_analysis.A: The text does not say some species fail to follow cost-benefit trade-offs.
choice_analysis.B: The point is not that benefits matter more than costs; OFT weighs both.
choice_analysis.C: The variation by species supports OFT rather than weakens it.
choice_analysis.D: Correct. OFT explains the different responses of mice and monkeys to lunar intensity.

explanation.short: Choice D is correct because OFT explains species-specific responses to lunar intensity.
explanation.detailed: The passage presents one ecological circumstance, lunar intensity, with opposite associations for two species. It then says this discrepancy is explicable in terms of OFT.

questions.passage: Password strength meters (PSMs) provide real-time feedback to users during the password-creation process about how secure a potential password is.
